Requirements:
- Implement exactly five cases and preserve the plan identifiers and categories.
- Give each case fresh setup, invoke production code and include a meaningful assertion.
- B1 must exercise the plan's below, at and above stimuli in the same case.

- Fakes may record calls and return fixed values; do not use mocking packages.

raw_plan_system_prompt:
You are planning regression characterisation tests for existing C# production code.
Work only from observable public behaviour in the pristine source and neutral dependency
context. Do not diagnose, improve, refactor or repair the production code.

Return ONLY one JSON object with suite_name and exactly five cases. Use these identifiers
and categories once each, in this order:
- H1 / happy_path: one representative valid end-to-end flow.
- E1 / empty_or_invalid: the most relevant empty, minimal, null or invalid-input flow.
- B1 / boundary_values: below, at and above one source-supported boundary. Put all three
  stimuli in inputs. If there is no numeric threshold, use the closest three-point
  cardinality or ordering boundary supported by the public contract.
- A1 / alternative_path: a materially different valid branch, mode or input partition.
- D1 / dependency_or_state: a deterministic dependency outcome, repeated invocation,
  duplicate input or state transition, choosing the first applicable option in that order.

Each case must contain case_id, category, source_evidence, input_partition, inputs and
expected_observation. Every input partition must differ. Evidence and expected observations
must describe behaviour visible in the supplied pristine code; do not invent requirements.
Do not include C# test code in this planning response.

cases.source_evidence: An item with a nonblank unique reference, matching currency, positive amount, no refund or hold, positive net, and net within the submission limit is accepted. When the gateway accepts, the method adds a submitted line and returns the accepted net as SubmittedTotal with BatchStatus "submitted".
cases.input_partition: Single fully eligible payment with calculated fees and an accepting gateway

cases.source_evidence: With no accepted entries, the method returns the accumulated lines, SubmittedTotal 0, and BatchStatus "empty" before inspecting the merchant or calling the gateway. An empty item collection produces no lines.

An otherwise eligible item is marked "batch-limit" only when the accumulated accepted net plus its net is strictly greater than submissionLimit. Therefore, a limit below the item's net rejects it, while limits equal to or above the net allow submission.
cases.input_partition: Submission limit immediately below, exactly at, and immediately above a single payment net of 10.00

cases.source_evidence: A held item is immediately represented by a zero-net "held" line, while another eligible item can still be submitted. After an accepted gateway response, the presence of any non-submitted line makes BatchStatus "partial". Deferred submitted lines are appended after previously recorded rejection lines.
cases.input_partition: Mixed batch containing one eligible payment and one held payment

cases.source_evidence: When the gateway returns Accepted false, every accepted payment is converted to a zero-net line whose status is "gateway-" followed by the gateway code. The method then returns SubmittedTotal 0 and BatchStatus "rejected".
cases.input_partition: Eligible payment followed by a deterministic gateway rejection
